topics.title: P & NP Classes
topics.content:
Complexity theory classifies computational problems based on the resources (time and space) required to solve them:

  • Class P (Polynomial Time): The class of decision problems that can be solved by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time \( O(n^k) \) for some constant \( k \) (e.g., searching, sorting, shortest paths).
  • Class NP (Nondeterministic Polynomial Time): The class of decision problems where a candidate solution can be verified by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time. If a problem is in P, it is also in NP (meaning \( P \subseteq NP \)).
topics.interviewTip: The P vs. NP question is one of the most famous unsolved problems in computer science. If asked, explain that 'P' represents problems that are easy to *solve*, while 'NP' represents problems that are easy to *verify* (once you are given a candidate solution).

topics.title: NP-Hard & NP-Complete Classes
topics.content:
To classify the hardest problems in NP, we use polynomial-time reductions:

  • NP-Hard: A problem \( X \) is NP-hard if any problem \( Y \in NP \) can be reduced to \( X \) in polynomial time. NP-hard problems do not have to be in NP themselves.
  • NP-Complete: A problem \( X \) is NP-complete if: (1) \( X \in NP \), and (2) \( X \) is NP-hard. They represent the hardest problems in NP. If any single NP-complete problem can be solved in polynomial time, then \( P = NP \).

topics.title: Cook's Theorem & Classic NPC Problems
topics.content:
Cook's Theorem (Cook-Levin Theorem): Proved that the Boolean Satisfiability Problem (SAT) is NP-complete. This was the first problem shown to be NP-complete, establishing the foundation of complexity theory. It proved that any NP problem can be represented as a SAT boolean formula.

Classic NP-Complete Problems:

  • 3-SAT: SAT restricted to 3 literals per clause.
  • Hamiltonian Path/Cycle: Finding a path/cycle in a graph that visits every vertex exactly once.
  • Vertex Cover: Finding a subset of vertices of size \( k \) that touches every edge in the graph.

topics.title: Approximation Algorithms
topics.content:
Since we cannot solve NP-complete problems optimally in polynomial time (unless \( P = NP \)), we use **Approximation Algorithms**. These are polynomial-time algorithms that find a solution that is close to the optimal solution.

An approximation algorithm has an **approximation ratio \( ho(n) \)** if for any input of size \( n \), the cost \( C \) of the solution satisfies: \[ \frac{1}{\rho(n)} \le \frac{C}{C^*} \le \rho(n) \] where \( C^* \) is the optimal cost. For example, there is a simple 2-approximation algorithm for the Vertex Cover problem based on matching edges.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the difference between Class P and Class NP?
practiceQuestions.answer: Class P consists of decision problems that can be solved in polynomial time by a deterministic Turing machine (e.g., finding a shortest path). Class NP consists of decision problems where a proposed solution can be verified in polynomial time by a deterministic Turing machine, even though finding the solution might take exponential time (e.g., Sudoku or Subset Sum).

practiceQuestions.question: Define NP-Complete and NP-Hard. How do they relate to each other?
practiceQuestions.answer: A problem is NP-Hard if every problem in NP can be reduced to it in polynomial time. A problem is NP-Complete if it is both in NP and is NP-Hard. Therefore, NP-Complete is the intersection of Class NP and NP-Hard. NP-Complete represents the hardest decision problems in NP.

practiceQuestions.question: State the significance of Cook's Theorem.
practiceQuestions.answer: Cook's Theorem proved that the Boolean Satisfiability Problem (SAT) is NP-complete. It was the first problem proven to be NP-complete. Its significance lies in the fact that it allows researchers to prove other problems are NP-complete simply by reducing SAT to them in polynomial time, rather than proving it from first principles.

practiceQuestions.question: What is a polynomial-time reduction? How is it used to prove NP-completeness?
practiceQuestions.answer: A polynomial-time reduction is a method of transforming problem A into problem B in polynomial time. To prove problem B is NP-complete: (1) we prove B is in NP, and (2) we select a known NP-complete problem A (like SAT or Vertex Cover) and show that A can be reduced to B in polynomial time. This implies that if we could solve B easily, we could also solve A easily.

practiceQuestions.question: What is an approximation algorithm? Define its approximation ratio.
practiceQuestions.answer: An approximation algorithm is a polynomial-time algorithm used to find near-optimal solutions to NP-hard optimization problems. Its performance is measured by its approximation ratio \( \rho(n) \), which bounds the ratio of the algorithm's solution cost to the absolute optimal solution cost.

mcqs.question: What does 'NP' stand for in complexity theory?
mcqs.explanation: NP stands for Nondeterministic Polynomial time, representing problems solvable in polynomial time by a nondeterministic Turing machine.

mcqs.question: If a problem is in Class P, then which of the following is also true?
options: It is NP-hard but not in NP
mcqs.explanation: Because any problem solvable in deterministic polynomial time is also verifiable in polynomial time, Class P is a subset of Class NP (\(P \subseteq NP\)).

mcqs.question: Which theorem proved that the Boolean Satisfiability Problem (SAT) is NP-complete?
mcqs.explanation: Cook's Theorem (or the Cook-Levin Theorem) established that SAT is NP-complete, marking the birth of NP-completeness theory.

mcqs.question: A problem X is NP-complete if:
options: X is in P and NP-hard
X is in NP and is NP-hard
X is NP-hard and cannot be verified
X can be solved in linear time
mcqs.explanation: By definition, a problem is NP-complete if it is in NP (verifiable in polynomial time) and is NP-hard (all NP problems reduce to it).

mcqs.question: Which of the following problems is NOT NP-complete?
mcqs.explanation: Dijkstra's single-source shortest path is in P because it can be solved in polynomial time \(O(E \log V)\).

mcqs.question: If an approximation algorithm for a minimization problem has an approximation ratio of 2, what does this mean?
options: The solution cost will be at most half of the optimal cost
The solution cost will be at most double the optimal cost
The algorithm takes twice as long to run
The algorithm uses twice as much memory
mcqs.explanation: For minimization, an approximation ratio of 2 (or a 2-approximation) guarantees the returned solution cost is at most 2 times the absolute minimum cost.

mcqs.question: A deterministic Turing machine is equivalent to which of the following?
options: A standard physical computer executing sequential instructions
A quantum computer executing infinite states
A system that runs without power
mcqs.explanation: A deterministic Turing machine models standard sequential computation where each state transition is uniquely determined.

mcqs.question: What is the relationship between NP-hard and NP-complete problems?
options: NP-hard is a subset of P
mcqs.explanation: NP-complete is a subset of NP-hard. A problem is NP-complete if it is NP-hard AND also belongs to Class NP.

mcqs.question: Reducing problem A to problem B in polynomial time implies:
options: A is harder than or equal to B
B is harder than or equal to A
They are both solvable in O(1) time
mcqs.explanation: Reducing A to B means we can use B's solver to solve A. Thus, B is at least as hard as A.

mcqs.question: The Hamiltonian Path problem asks if a graph contains a path that:
options: Connects all vertices with minimum edge weights
mcqs.explanation: A Hamiltonian Path visits every vertex in the graph exactly once. (Visiting every edge exactly once is an Eulerian Path).
